evidence_note: Pompey's father. Consul 89 BCE. Died 87 BCE.
Pompey raised legions for Sulla in 83 BCE. Sulla gave him commands, arranged marriages (Antistia divorced, Aemilia Scaura arranged), and greeted him as imperator.
Rivals competing for credit over Spartacus (71 BCE); co-consuls (70 BCE); political allies in 'First Triumvirate' (60-53 BCE); rivalry reignited after Julia's death and Crassus's eastern ambitions.

Political ally via 'First Triumvirate' (60-54 BCE); son-in-law through marriage to Julia (59 BCE); opponent/rival in civil war (49-48 BCE). Florus: 'Pompey could not brook an equal, or Caesar a superior.'
Fourth wife (married April 59 BCE). Daughter of Julius Caesar. Her death in childbirth (September 54 BCE) removed a key personal bond between Pompey and Caesar.
Cicero supported Pompey's extraordinary commands (Pro Lege Manilia, 66 BCE) and backed him as praefectus annonae (57 BCE). Later ambivalent; made peace with Caesar after Pharsalus.
Often opposed Pompey's extraordinary commands and eastern settlement ratification; backed Pompey as sole consul (52 BCE). Announced intention to continue war from Africa after Pharsalus.
Ptolemy XIII's court ordered Pompey's assassination upon his arrival at Pelusium in 48 BCE. Ptolemy was a minor (age 14); the decision was made by his advisors.
Elder son by Mucia Tertia. Born c.75 BCE. Fought at Munda (45 BCE); executed after capture on 12 April 45 BCE.
Younger son by Mucia Tertia. Born c.67 BCE. Formed last organized opposition to Second Triumvirate; established independent state in Sicily; executed 35 BCE.
Fifth and final wife (married 52 BCE). Daughter of Metellus Scipio. Widowed by Pompey's death; received his ashes for burial.
Third wife (married c.79 BCE). Mother of Gnaeus, Pompeia, and Sextus. Divorced 61 BCE (reason disputed: adultery or political expediency).
